$comment: One English word, two things. `scale` in this corpus is the weighing balance — pivoted beam, pan at each end — and three recipes were using it to make a moth's wing, a reptile's skin and a shark's hide. Every one of those `why` texts was about the right thing; only the gesture underneath was about a set of kitchen scales. That is the project's own fault class, sitting in the middle of the corpus behind prose good enough to hide it, and nothing could see it, because an element id carries no sense. This file gives each ambiguous word its declared sense and the words that betray a different one, so the check is precise and the corpus cannot drift back.
$rules: sense is the meaning THIS corpus uses for that element. It should be recognisable in the element's own fact; if it is not, the fact is the thing to fix.
not lists lowercase markers for the OTHER senses. A recipe using the element whose why contains one of them is an error, because the prose and the gesture are then talking about different things.

also names the elements that carry the other senses, so the fix for a flagged recipe is already in the file. An `also` id that does not exist is an error — it means a sense was split out and then lost.
allow names outputs where the crossing is deliberate and understood, with a reason. It must be used sparingly: an allow entry is a claim that a human looked at that specific recipe.

cleared is the other half of the denominator: single-word element names reviewed and found to carry one sense only. Coverage is watched + cleared out of every single-word name used in two or more recipes — measured against the whole vocabulary, not against the words that happened to be interesting.

allow.why: seed + wing. A samara's blade is grown, not built, so it is neither of the animal senses and not strictly a cambered aerofoil either — but it is a lifting surface that autorotates, and the recipe's why is about exactly that. Splitting a third wing element for one recipe would be worse than saying here that this crossing was looked at.

watch.found: 31 of 36 recipes taking `wing` meant a bird's, an insect's or a god's — wing+moon→owl, wing+zeus→hypnos, insect+wing→beetle, chitin+wing→wing_scale, keratin+wing→flight_feather — while the element itself is an aircraft wing made from wing_spar + canvas. The largest single sense fault found so far.
